Consult Summary:
- Acute, persistent headache for three days with photophobia and mild visual phenomena; assessment plans include neurological/examination workup and analgesic optimization; possible migraine suspected.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Blinding headache present for three days, interfering with work and concentration.
- Onset and course: Sudden onset upon waking three days ago; persistent since, with partial relief from Ibuprofen but not resolution.
- Pain characteristics: Global headache with right-eye emphasis; severity reported as 8/10 at worst, down to ~5/10 with Ibuprofen.
- Aggravating/relieving factors: Light exposure worsens symptoms (photophobia); standing up quickly may cause stabbing pain; head movement described as a sensation of internal movement; Ibuprofen provides partial relief; sleep generally good.
- Associated symptoms: Light sensitivity and transient visual phenomena described as “shooting light” and odd vision; no nausea or vomiting; no fever; no nasal/sinus symptoms; no coughing or blood in sputum.
- Past headaches: Previously occasional; one recent 2-day episode resolved with Ibuprofen; no long-standing headache pattern.
- Medical history: Childhood pain reported that resolved; no chronic medical conditions documented.
- Medications: Ibuprofen for headaches; Oral contraceptive pill started about 1 year ago; no other medications listed.
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Lives alone; works from home; non-smoker; alcohol use approximately 3 units per week (regular; details not fully specified); no other illicit drug use.
- Family history: Mother has migraines with vomiting; no other family history noted.
- Review of systems: Generally negative aside from headaches and photophobia; no recent weight change, fever, or systemic symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- Recurrent or past headaches: occasional; one 2-day episode previously resolved with Ibuprofen.
- Other: Childhood pain history with resolution; no chronic illnesses documented.
- Oral contraceptive pill started ~1 year ago; no documented adverse effects.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen (for headaches) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Oral contraceptive pill — dose/brand/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: None.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Smoking: No.
- Alcohol: Regular use; approximately 3 units per week.
- Other drugs: None noted.

Family History:
- Mother with migraines (migraine with vomiting); no other notable family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- Recent eye examination: Vision unchanged; no acute findings reported.
- Other investigations: none documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute probable migraine-type headache with photophobia and mild visual symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Schedule a full neurological examination and ophthalmoscopic assessment (fundoscopy) via appointment with the support line; examination to be performed to evaluate for red flags and visual involvement.
    - Start a stronger analgesic option than Ibuprofen; exact agent name to be determined (described as a medication similar to Ibuprofen but stronger); dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Continue Paracetamol as an adjunct (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Instruct to take the new medication with food.
    - If symptoms worsen, are unbearable, or new red-flag symptoms develop, go to A&E.
    - Blood pressure to be checked at the appointment.
- Issue 2: Contraception considerations given migraine features.
  - Plan:
    - Review suitability of the oral contraceptive pill at the appointment; if migraine with aura or flashing lights persists, discuss potential change of contraception.
    - Ensure BP check is performed to support any changes in therapy.
- General Plan:
  - If headache improves and the appointment is canceled, no further action needed; otherwise proceed with the scheduled examination and management.
